## Purpose

This SOP describes the laboratory procedures for identifying and
enumerating benthic algae (periphyton) from stream bioassessment
samples. Periphyton assemblages are sensitive indicators of water
quality, nutrient enrichment, and physical habitat condition, and are
a required component of the California SWAMP bioassessment protocol
[@ode2016; @barbour1999]. This SOP covers soft-bodied algae (green
algae, cyanobacteria, and other non-diatom taxa) and diatoms, which
are processed separately due to different preparation requirements
[@charles2002; @stevenson1996].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Identification and enumeration of benthic periphyton
  from composite epilithic, epiphytic, or epidendric samples collected
  per SWAMP protocols at EA Program stream sites
- **Does not apply to:** Phytoplankton (water column) identification;
  chlorophyll *a* extraction (see
  [SOP-L310](SOP-L310-chlorophyll-extraction.qmd)); algal culture or
  toxin analysis; molecular identification (eDNA metabarcoding)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Lab Manager  | Approve taxonomic protocols; arrange external QC        |
| Trained Personnel | Process samples, identify and enumerate algae           |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent identification     |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Lugol's iodine solution (preservative) contains
  potassium iodide and iodine; it is a mild irritant and stains skin
  and clothing. Nitric acid (used in diatom cleaning) is corrosive;
  handle in the fume hood. The mounting medium Naphrax contains
  toluene, which is flammable and toxic by inhalation.
- **Physical:** Hot plates used for diatom cleaning and slide
  preparation pose burn risk. Coverslips and slides are fragile.
- **Biological:** Stream samples may contain pathogens. Wear gloves.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or goggles
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Fume hood (required for nitric acid cleaning and Naphrax mounting)

### Emergency Procedures

For acid splashes, flush immediately with copious water for at least
15 minutes. For Naphrax/toluene spills, ventilate and absorb. Refer
to [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

| Compound microscope (brightfield)     | 400x and 1000x (oil immersion) for diatoms |
| Inverted microscope (optional)        | For soft-bodied algae in settling chambers |
| Palmer-Maloney counting cell          | For soft-bodied algae enumeration        |
| Hot plate                             | For diatom acid cleaning                 |
| Centrifuge                            | For concentrating cleaned diatom material |
| Slide warmer                          | For drying diatom mounts                 |

### Consumables

| Item                              | Notes                              |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| Lugol's iodine solution           | Preservative for soft-bodied algae |
| Concentrated HNO~3~ (trace metal grade) | For diatom frustule cleaning  |
| 30% H~2~O~2~                     | Alternative oxidizer for cleaning  |
| Naphrax mounting medium           | High refractive index (n = 1.73); for permanent diatom slides |
| Coverslips (22 x 22 mm, No. 1)   |                                    |
| Glass microscope slides           |                                    |
| Immersion oil                     |                                    |


## Procedure

### Sample Processing Overview

Periphyton samples are processed in two parallel workflows:

1. **Soft-bodied algae:** Examined alive or preserved in Lugol's
   solution using a Palmer-Maloney cell or settling chamber at
   400x magnification.
2. **Diatoms:** Cleaned with acid or peroxide to remove organic matter,
   mounted in Naphrax on permanent slides, and identified at 1000x
   (oil immersion).

### Soft-Bodied Algae Identification

1. Homogenize the preserved sample by gently inverting the jar 20
   times.
2. Pipette a known volume (typically 0.1 mL) into a Palmer-Maloney
   counting cell.
3. Allow cells to settle for 5 minutes.
4. Scan the entire cell at 400x magnification.
5. Identify and count a minimum of 300 natural units (cells, colonies,
   or filament lengths of 10 $\mu$m). A natural unit is the smallest
   entity that can be identified: a single cell for unicellular taxa,
   a colony for colonial taxa, or a 10 $\mu$m filament segment for
   filamentous taxa [@stevenson1996].
6. Record counts by taxon. Identify to genus where possible; use
   higher-level groupings (family or order) for taxa that cannot be
   resolved without specialized preparation.
7. Calculate cell density:

$$
\text{Cells/cm}^2 = \frac{N \times V_{\text{sample}}}{V_{\text{counted}} \times A_{\text{substrate}}}
$$

where $N$ = number of cells counted, $V_{\text{sample}}$ = total
sample volume (mL), $V_{\text{counted}}$ = volume examined in the
counting cell (mL), and $A_{\text{substrate}}$ = total area of
substrate scraped in the field (cm^2^).

### Diatom Cleaning

1. Transfer approximately 5 mL of well-mixed sample to a labeled
   glass beaker or test tube.
2. In the fume hood, add an equal volume of concentrated HNO~3~
   (or 30% H~2~O~2~ as a less hazardous alternative).
3. Heat on the hot plate at low-to-medium heat (approximately 80 °C)
   until the sample clears and all organic material is digested
   (30--60 minutes). Do not boil.
4. Allow to cool. Centrifuge at 1500 x g for 5 minutes and decant
   the supernatant.
5. Wash the pellet with DI water, centrifuge, and decant. Repeat the
   wash 3--5 times until the pH of the supernatant is near neutral.
6. Resuspend the cleaned frustules in a small volume of DI water
   (approximately 1--2 mL).

### Diatom Slide Preparation

1. Pipette a drop of cleaned diatom suspension onto a clean coverslip.
   Allow to air-dry completely on the slide warmer.
2. Place a drop of Naphrax on a labeled glass slide (work in the fume
   hood; Naphrax contains toluene).
3. Invert the coverslip (diatom side down) onto the Naphrax drop.
4. Heat gently on the hot plate or slide warmer to drive off the
   toluene until no more bubbles appear.
5. Allow to cool. The slide is now a permanent mount.

### Diatom Identification and Enumeration

1. Examine the slide at 1000x under oil immersion.
2. Count a minimum of 600 diatom valves, traversing random transects
   across the coverslip [@charles2002].
3. Identify each valve to the lowest practical taxonomic level (species
   where possible) using regional diatom floras and SWAMP reference
   keys [@krammer2000; @spaulding2021].
4. Record counts by taxon.

### Data Entry and Metric Calculation

1. Enter soft-bodied and diatom counts into the standardized data
   entry spreadsheet.
2. Calculate summary metrics: total taxa richness, relative abundance
   of indicator taxa (e.g., pollution-tolerant vs. sensitive diatoms),
   and community-level indices.
3. If submitting to SWAMP/CEDEN, format data per SWAMP requirements.


## Quality Control

- **Soft-bodied algae:** Re-count 10% of samples. Counts should agree
  within 15% RPD for dominant taxa.
- **Diatoms:** Have a second identifier verify 10% of slides. Taxonomic
  agreement should be greater than or equal to 85% at the species
  level.
- For SWAMP submissions, submit 10% of diatom slides to a
  SWAMP-certified taxonomist for external QC.
- Include a reference slide set in the laboratory for training and
  calibration.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Nitric acid waste             | Neutralize and collect in acid waste; EH&S pickup |
| H~2~O~2~ waste               | Dilute and drain with copious water      |
| Naphrax / toluene waste       | Collect in organic waste; EH&S pickup    |
| Lugol's iodine waste          | Collect in designated container; EH&S pickup |
| Used slides and coverslips    | Standard sharps/glass waste              |

## Training Record

Before identifying and enumerating algae independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   training
3. Review the SDS for nitric acid and Naphrax
4. Study the diatom and soft-bodied algae reference collections and
   identification keys
5. Complete a supervised identification exercise (minimum 100 diatom
   valves and 50 soft-bodied algae natural units) with greater than
   80% agreement with reference identifications
6. Demonstrate safe acid cleaning and Naphrax mounting under
   supervision
7. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
